title: Cycling — full pedalling analysis (Tour de France warm-up)
blurb: Real handheld footage, whole 30 s clip: hip, knee and foot tracked; knee angle, crank angle, cadence, foot speed; wheel calibration corrects the bike being at an angle; camera motion compensated.

tour.title: A finished analysis
tour.text: Real handheld footage from the Tour de France: the yellow-jersey rider's leg is tracked for the whole 30-second clip — Hip, Knee and the Shoe (on its dials). Press Space to play. Use Next to walk through it.

tour.title: The timeline: what's measured where
tour.text: One lane per point. Own colour = tracked confidently. Orange = less certain: blurry frames where the match was weaker, plus a few per stroke filled in by interpolation. Empty = not measured: around 5 s someone walks in front of the camera and around 20 s a team car drives through — no point guessing there, so the graphs have gaps too. White ticks = keyframes placed by hand to restart tracking after those.

tour.title: Why there's an ellipse on the wheel
tour.text: The bike isn't side-on: it's turned about 54° away from the camera (the round wheel looks like a tall, thin ellipse). A simple scale line would make every sideways distance ~40% too short and the angles wrong. So this uses a Wheel calibration: the 4 yellow dots sit on the tyre's tan stripe (0.64 m across). From the ellipse the app works out the bike's angle and measures in the bike's plane, as if filmed side-on.

tour.title: What x and y mean here
tour.text: Positions are in metres in the bike's plane. (0, 0) is where the front wheel touches the ground. y (green arrow) is height above the ground. x (red arrow) runs along the bike, towards the back wheel (this rider faces left). So Shoe y ≈ 0.25–0.6 m is how high the foot is.

tour.title: The camera moves — the app follows it
tour.text: This was filmed handheld, so the picture shifts and zooms. Camera moves — follow it (ticked in Calibration) measures that on every frame and cancels it out. Watch the yellow wheel outline: it stays glued to the wheel while the camera moves. Without this, the camera's own movement would be counted as the rider moving.

tour.title: Knee angle
tour.text: The white arc: the angle at the knee between hip and foot, in the bike's plane. It swings between about 85° (most bent, top of the stroke) and 152° (most straight, bottom) every pedal stroke. This frame is the most bent. Hover the graph to read values; click it to jump the video there.

tour.title: Most extended
tour.text: Leg at its straightest. All current values are under At this frame. (It's measured to the shoe's dials rather than the ankle bone — the white sock can't be tracked reliably — so treat it as a few degrees approximate.)

tour.title: Cadence from the crank angle
tour.text: Crank is a fixed point at the centre of the foot's circle (≈ the crank axle). Crank angle is the tilt of Crank→Shoe; the graph shows how fast it turns: about 523°/s, i.e. 87 rpm — a typical warm-up cadence. (360°/s = 60 rpm.)

tour.title: Foot speed
tour.text: Because it's calibrated, speeds are real: the foot moves at about 1.2 m/s around its circle. Switch the dropdown to Position Y to see the foot going up and down.

tour.title: Filled-in frames
tour.text: At the back of each stroke the foot is too blurred to match, so a few frames per stroke were filled by interpolation (Edit → Fill gaps) — shown orange on the timeline and as a small dot instead of a ring on the video. Long gaps (blocked view) are left empty on purpose.

tour.title: How the tracker is set up
tour.text: With a point selected you see two boxes: the solid box is the patch it looks for each frame, the dotted box is how far it searches. Tracking settings: Min. match (how sure it must be before it stops to ask), Bridge gaps (coast through short hidden spells), snapping clicks onto markers, and re-tracking after you fix something.

tour.title: Right-click for more
tour.text: Right-click a point for: delete it on this frame, clear everything after here, fill gaps, or track only this point. Right-click empty space to add a point. Right-drag pans; the wheel zooms; F fits.

tour.title: Try it: track something new
tour.text: The + Point tool is on. Click the green-jersey rider's white shoe (left of the yellow rider), then press Track ▶ (T). If it stops and asks, press Enter to accept its guess or click the right spot. Esc returns to Select. Ctrl+Z undoes anything.
